items.text: We started using the document QA assistant for our release notes review last quarter and it's been a quiet improvement over the old grep-and-pray approach. It parses the changelog, the migration guide and the API diff in one go, and I can ask things like "which endpoints changed signature in 4.2" and get a straight answer with citations. The system still stumbles on tables pasted from Confluence, but nothing's perfect. For a small team with no dedicated release manager it saves a couple of hours per cycle.

Invoice INV-20841 from Harrowgate Supplies arrived with the wrong PO reference and a line item we never ordered, so I flagged it back to their accounts team. They were apologetic and said an override had been applied manually on their side, which is why the totals didn't reconcile. It's the third time this quarter, so I've asked our admin coordinator to put them on a watch list. Not urgent, but worth tracking. The desk we did order showed up fine, at least.

Long post, sorry. I run procurement for a mid-size logistics firm and we've been trialing one of these document assistants against our vendor contracts. The pitch is that you dump in the master services agreement plus all the amendments and ask plain questions — "what's our termination notice period with Brightwell Freight", "does the indemnity cap apply to data breaches". It mostly works, and when it cites the clause it's usually right. But the failure mode that bit me is it silently preferring the newest amendment even when a later side letter partially overrides it. We caught it because a renewal date was off by two months and that's exactly the kind of thing that gets missed when people stop reading the contract.

Second thing: the system is only as good as what you feed it. We had a scanned PDF with the signature pages missing and it just answered confidently from the half it had. No warning, no "I couldn't read page 12". If you're going to rely on this for anything with money attached, keep a human reviewer on the urgent items at least, and treat admin changes to the document set like a change to the answer.

Overall I'd recommend it for triage and search, not for final sign-off. The tool that shows its citations inline is worth the extra licence cost; the one that just answers is a trap.

Quick review of the 3.1 release for anyone running the self-hosted version: the document QA chatbot now handles supplier invoice PDFs with multi-page tables without choking, which used to be our biggest complaint. Indexing is maybe 20% faster. There's a known issue where the OCR fallback kicks in on already-text PDFs and doubles the processing time — devs say a patch is coming. We've been on it a week in staging and haven't seen anything scary. Would upgrade again.

Context: we're a 40-person agency and reviewed three document assistants for contract and invoice work. Writing this up because I wish someone had for me.

Accuracy: all three got the easy extraction questions right (party names, dates, payment terms). Differences showed up on conditional clauses and cross-references. The two tools that show the source paragraph side by side were far easier to trust; the one that just summarised was often subtly wrong and we couldn't tell without reading the original anyway. So the override on our shortlist went to the transparent ones.

Admin and setup: importing a folder of supplier invoices took an afternoon, mostly fixing bad scan names. One vendor wanted an urgent call with their sales engineer before they'd let us trial the contract module, which was a bit much. Pricing ran from about £40 to £300 a month for our volume.

Verdict: the mid-priced tool with citations won. The cheap one is fine for invoice lookup alone, and the expensive one is really built for legal teams with a reviewing workflow we don't have.

Vendor contract renewal is coming up with Pallister & Vane and I've been using the assistant to pull together the key dates and obligations. It found the change-of-control clause and the auto-renewal window in about ten seconds, both of which I'd forgotten about. It did get confused by one schedule that references an earlier version, but I checked and it was my file that was wrong. Worth noting for the admin team: re-upload the final signed copy, not the draft.

On supplier invoices the bot is honestly great at the boring stuff — pulling the PO number, spotting a duplicate, telling me which ones are overdue. What it won't do is make a judgement call on whether a partial delivery should be paid, and I don't want it to. The system flags exceptions and I deal with them. Small gripe: the admin dashboard for uploading new invoice batches is clunky and the override for re-processing a failed file is buried three menus deep. Otherwise no complaints from me.

Reviewing the document QA assistant from the perspective of a legal ops team, since there wasn't much written by people actually using it on vendor contracts.

The good: search across a folder of MSAs and statements of work is genuinely fast, and asking "which suppliers have a liability cap under £250k" is the kind of question that used to mean an afternoon with a spreadsheet. Answers come with links to the exact clause, which makes review quick. For bulk triage before a renewal round, this thing earns its keep.

Where it falls short: anything that requires reconciling two documents against each other. Ask it whether an SOW override conflicts with the master agreement and you'll get a plausible answer that is right maybe 70% of the time. That's not good enough for sign-off, so we treat it as a first pass only. We also had to sort out who counts as admin in the tool, because by default anyone could delete a contract set and that's an urgent audit finding waiting to happen. Pricing was reasonable for five seats.

If you buy it expecting a reviewer rather than a search engine, you'll be happy. Expect it to replace your contracts admin and you'll get burned.
The new release finally fixes the invoice table parsing, which was the main reason our team kept falling back to manual checks.
Anyone else find the contract module's admin console confusing when you need to override a document's retained version? Looking for tips before our vendor renewal crunch next month.
